newsitem.title: UK: NWE spot gasoline steady, swaps firmer after APIs.
newsitem.headline: NWE spot gasoline steady, swaps firmer after APIs.

text.p: NWE spot gasoline prices were steady on Wednesday with barges supported by short covering while bullish API data underpinned cargoes, traders said.
Weekly stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) were viewed slightly constructive but some doubts were expressed over the data's validity.
"The data is a bit weird," one futures trader said.

The API figures showed "implied demand" for gasoline at a record 8.76 million barrels per day (bpd), in contrast to recent data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) which showed year-to-date gasoline demand has been "underwhelming" this year.

"It would be a surprise if gasoline extended substantially higher today purely on the API data," GNI research said in a daily report. "We need to see how the EIA figures compare, to make a better assessment."

Eurograde gasoline barges traded at $194 fob Rotterdam twice as a German buyer sought to cover ahead of an extended weekend. Later offers were at that level and those for the whole of May at $195 fob.
Some players were surprised the market was not higher after bullish U.S. stocks figures. However forward price indicators May swaps saw offers rise a couple of dollars to $196 a tonne fob ARA.
U.S. gasoline stocks fell 3.6 million to 190.5 million barrels last week and were some 13.2 million barrels below last years already low levels. Imports totalled some 473,000 barrels per day.
They speculated that Thursday's European holidays and the likely lack of players on Friday was partly to blame for a lull in trading.
